automation_name: AI Security Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Include only public items published or visibly updated within the last 2 days relative to run time; exclude missing, ambiguous, future-dated, or boundary-only dates.

searched_topics: agent and tool security including MCP, plugins, browsers, delegated authority, and autonomous action
identity, authentication, authorization, credentials, and least privilege
model, dataset, dependency, artifact, runtime, cloud, hardware, and deployment supply chains
threat modeling, red teaming, security evaluation, assurance, monitoring, and release gates
AI security standards, regulation, governance, audit evidence, and risk management
public AI security incidents, mitigations, patches, disclosures, and lessons learned

routing_context.local_security_wiki: Owns AI-specific security findings, affected boundaries, mitigations, assurance implications, and incident lessons.
routing_context.upstream_ai_wiki: Owns broad AI companies, models, products, frameworks, MCP servers, developer tools, and general techniques.
routing_context.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: Owns general AI-assisted development practices, coding-agent workflows, verification patterns, adoption practices, and development governance.

collection_methods: Read automation memory before collection to avoid repeating recent focus.
Checked ai-security-wiki federation rules and upstream ai-wiki and ai-dev-wiki topic indexes for routing context.

Ran paced NVD CVE API keyword searches over the exact lastModified window for AI, MCP, LLM, prompt, agent, LangChain, LiteLLM, Open WebUI, Flowise, Copilot, model, embedding, RAG, ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini.
Fetched direct CVEAWG records and NVD records for selected CVEs to verify public timestamps, affected versions, descriptions, and reference URLs.
Used public web searches and direct source pages for in-window public incident/research candidates.
Searched raw, raw/processed, and docs/wiki locally for selected IDs before classifying findings as fresh collector output.
privacy_and_source_boundary: Public web sources only. No private, proprietary, sensitive, PII, or company-internal local content was sent to an external service. docs/wiki was not edited.

qualifying_findings.title: Contentful MCP Server exposes LLM-controlled network options in migration tools
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Contentful MCP Server before @contentful/mcp-server 1.7.19 and @contentful/mcp-tools 0.4.5 allowed export_space and import_space to pass LLM-controlled host, proxy, rawProxy, and insecure network options into Contentful Management API requests.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE record and NVD vulnerability record
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Contentful MCP Server and @contentful/mcp-server before 1.7.19; @contentful/mcp-tools before 0.4.5; MCP migration tools and outbound Contentful Management API request boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Tool arguments generated or selected by an LLM can redirect server-side network requests and expose management tokens unless MCP tools separate model-controlled parameters from privileged client configuration.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the LLM-controlled network-option boundary and MCP credential-risk implication in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: Contentful and broad MCP server/product context are upstream-owned if durable entity background is needed.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General MCP migration workflow guidance belongs upstream only when not security-specific.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: direct CVEAWG and NVD timestamps are inside the run window.

qualifying_findings.title: Flowise chat-model baseURL validation gap can exfiltrate LLM provider keys
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Flowise before 3.1.4 failed to validate baseURL parameters in chat-model nodes, allowing authenticated users with chatflows:create or chatflows:update permissions to redirect requests to arbitrary hosts and exfiltrate LLM provider API keys.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE record and NVD vulnerability record
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Flowise and flowise-components before 3.1.4; chat-model node request destination validation and provider credential boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Low-code LLM builders often hold provider credentials; redirectable model-node traffic can turn ordinary builder permissions into key exfiltration and internal-host access.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the credential-exfiltration and model-node destination-control lesson in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: Flowise as a broad low-code LLM product/framework is upstream-owned for general background.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General low-code LLM workflow usage belongs upstream unless framed as a security gate.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: CVEAWG publication and NVD update are inside the exact run window.

qualifying_findings.title: MCP Memory Keeper context_import allows path traversal into server-readable files
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: MCP Memory Keeper before 0.13.0 passed caller-controlled filePath directly to fs.readFileSync in context_import without restricting it to an export directory, letting an MCP client or induced LLM agent use traversal or absolute paths to import files readable by the server process.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE record and NVD vulnerability record
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mkreyman mcp-memory-keeper before 0.13.0; context_import file-read boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Persistent memory tools are high-risk agent context surfaces; unsafe import paths can leak local files into an agent session and then into downstream model/tool flows.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the MCP memory-file boundary and induced-agent file-read implication in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: MCP Memory Keeper as a tool entity is upstream-owned if broad tool catalog context is needed.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General memory-tool workflow guidance belongs upstream when not vulnerability-specific.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: direct CVEAWG and NVD timestamps are inside the run window.

qualifying_findings.title: LiteLLM nested user_config api_base bypass enables SSRF-style request redirection
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: LiteLLM before 1.83.9 allowed an authenticated proxy caller with a valid virtual key to place api_base inside user_config, bypassing checks that blocked top-level api_base and base_url and redirecting outbound router requests to attacker-selected internal or external hosts.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE record and NVD vulnerability record
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: BerriAI LiteLLM before 1.83.9; proxy virtual-key request-body validation and outbound router destination boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI gateways mediate credentials and model traffic; nested configuration fields need the same destination controls as top-level fields or authenticated tenants can pivot through the gateway.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the AI-gateway request-redirection and virtual-key boundary finding in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: LiteLLM as a broad AI proxy/gateway entity is upstream-owned for general product context.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General model-routing operations belong upstream unless tied to security controls.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: direct CVEAWG and NVD publication timestamps are inside the run window.

qualifying_findings.title: macOS Golden Gate fixes secure-prompt clickjacking bypass
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Apple fixed a macOS issue in Golden Gate 27 where a malicious app could bypass clickjacking protections for secure prompts; the CVE record says improved state management addressed the issue.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE record with NVD update corroboration
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Apple macOS versions before Golden Gate 27; secure-prompt clickjacking protection boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Assistant and secure-prompt UI boundaries depend on clickjacking-resistant consent flows; local app bypasses can weaken human approval gates around sensitive actions.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the secure-prompt approval-boundary implication in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: Broad Apple Intelligence/macOS product context belongs upstream if needed.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General approval UX practice belongs upstream only when not tied to this security fix.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Moderate-high confidence: original publication was before the exact window, but the primary CVE record and NVD both show visible in-window updates.

qualifying_findings.title: CrowdStrike reports LLM-generated PhantomRaven npm information stealer used for bug bounty hunting
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: CrowdStrike Counter Adversary Operations identified PhantomRaven, a JavaScript information stealer distributed through npm packages; CrowdStrike assesses with high confidence that the malware was likely LLM-generated based on verbose comments, placeholder code, and statistical token-analysis patterns. The malware collected system, runtime, Git/npm identity, and CI/CD environment data and exfiltrated it by HTTP GET and POST.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary security research report with secondary reputable news corroboration
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: npm dependency installation and JavaScript package supply chain; malicious packages identified by CrowdStrike include transform-jsbi-to-bigint and sort-imports-es6-autofix.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The report is a concrete public example of LLM-assisted malware lowering the barrier for software supply-chain compromise and credential collection from development and CI/CD environments.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the AI-assisted malware and development-supply-chain credential-risk implication in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: CrowdStrike company background and broad AI threat-intelligence product context are upstream-owned if needed.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General developer package-install workflow guidance belongs upstream; security-specific npm malware lessons remain local.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for the public report and date. Attribution to LLM generation remains CrowdStrike's assessment, not independently reproduced in this run.
